concept.name: Futures contract
concept.definition: A standardized exchange-traded agreement obligating parties to buy or sell an underlying interest at a future time under contract terms, commonly settled through offset or delivery and cleared with daily margining.
concept.intuition: It defines the legal and economic claim being traded, including who must perform and when.
concept.mechanics: The exchange specifies size, tick, expiry, and settlement; the clearinghouse novates trades, marks positions to market, and collects margin.
concept.failure_modes: Counterparty, settlement, liquidity, exercise, basis, and leverage terms differ by venue and contract and can dominate the apparent payoff.
concept.misconceptions: Similar price exposure does not make spot, forwards, futures, and options operationally or legally interchangeable.
concept.example: One crude-oil future represents the contract quantity for a stated month; daily gains and losses flow through variation margin.
